ops.title: stack submit: lane = stack-new lineage via a ccx-lane id in the worktree admin dir, not path or session id
ops.body:
PR #250. Report (pr-comment-parity, 2026-10-02 8:30 PM PT): worktree add P, stack new child from inside P, then stack submit from the child kept P with "another lane owns them". Ownership was holder path != invoking root.

CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID cannot name a lane. Every in-process subagent or teammate of a drive inherits the ROOT session id: all subagent transcripts live under the root session dir, and no per-agent env var exists in Bash. Using it would merge every lane in a drive.

Rule now: when stack new cuts a child onto the non-trunk branch the invoking worktree has checked out, it writes a random lane id (crypto/rand.Text) into <child GitDir>/ccx-lane. It mints that id into the source admin dir first if the source has none. vcs.Lane(c) is the recorded id, else c.Root. vcs.ForeignBranchHolders drops holders whose lane equals ours. Prunable holders stay foreign. jj workspaces never read a record, because their GitDir is the shared one. Two sites use it: runStackSubmit, and stackPinHeldParents for receipt-restored parents. The finder caught that second site.

The id is random, not the founder path, because a worktree recreated at the founder path would otherwise inherit the lane (finder repro). These worktrees found their own lane, with protection unchanged: raw git worktree add, ccx worktree add, stack new --parent X from a checkout not holding X, and anything cut onto trunk.

Tests: TestStackSubmitTakesTheParentAnotherWorkingCopyOfThisLaneHolds (red before, with the exact message), ...KeepsTheParentAWorkingCopyOfAnotherLaneHolds, ...RecreatedAtTheFoundersPath, ...TakesAPublishedParent..., and TestStackNewOntoTrunkFoundsALane. The stackLane helper now cuts from a detached sibling checkout so it stays another lane. Local test runs need PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin first, because the mise gt shim is broken, and the wasm artifacts copied from the main checkout.
